ov: A lizard-like reptile found only in New Zealand, and the last survivor of the order Rhynchocephalia, the dominant group of small reptiles in the Jurassic. Tuatara stay active at temperatures as low as 5 °C, much colder than most reptiles tolerate. The name is Māori for "peaks on the back".
len: Males about 61 cm; females about 45 cm
wt: Males up to 1 kg; females up to 0.5 kg
rg: New Zealand, mainly on 32 offshore islands, with fenced sanctuaries on the mainland.
df: Mostly beetles, crickets, spiders, wētā, earthworms and snails, plus frogs, lizards and seabird eggs and chicks.
fx: It has a light-sensing third eye on top of its head, visible only in hatchlings.
The average lifespan is about 60 years, and tuatara can live to well over 100.
